org.name: Norfolk and Suffolk NHS Foundation Trust

hazard: Lack of automated discharge medication notification
theme: Alcohol, drug and medication related deaths

reports.title: Rachel Edwards: Prevention of future deaths report
categories: Alcohol, drug and medication related deaths

promises.quote: The Trust will make an assessment of the medications prescribed upon discharge and this consideration will continue across the Trust.
promises.summary: Assess discharge medications across the Trust

concerns.quote: Prior to Rachel's death, on the 6th March 2017 she was informally admitted to the Woodlands mental health ward In Ipswich following a significant overdose she had taken on the 3rd March 2017
concerns.hazard: stockpiling of medication leading to overdose

concerns.quote: It was known that Rachel was at risk of stockpiling medication as in the Serious Incident Requiring Investigation (SIRI) report it is noted that a request made on the 7th March 2017 by her treating doctor, for the disposal of her stocks of medication had not been actioned

Such confusion over the actual quantities of medication Issued and the apparent issuing of 14 days supply of medicines to a patient who is known to have previously stockpiled medication, with a View to self-harm, is of obvious concern
there is no automated notification to a patient's GP of the type and amounts of prescription medicines issued to a patient upon discharge from Woodlands
concerns.hazard: lack of automated discharge medication notification

concerns.quote: no 'patient advocate' or other similar service in place to act as filter and alert those providing support to prepare for the increased feeling of hopelessness that would clearly follow such news
no formal system in place for an advocate to be appointed in other cases when it could prove beneficial
concerns.hazard: lack of formal patient advocate appointment process

reports.title: Ellie Long
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

promises.quote: The Trust is taking the following actions which are anticipated to assist in bringing consistent and sustained improvement. All clinical services have been instructed to review their working practice in respect of record keeping and communication with partner agencies. Responsibility for this rests with the operational managers who will provide assurance of the actions taken to drive improvement.
promises.summary: All clinical services must review record keeping and communication practices; operational managers will assure implementation.

concerns.quote: Not all records were properly recorded on Lorenzo. Further, personal handwritten notes were made of some meetings which were not then reflected in the electronic records. Some of these notes only came to light during the inquest hearing. It is, of course, imperative that all staff recognise their obligations in respect of keeping full and contemporaneous electronic records and that full disclosure of all relevant documents is made in a timely fashion before the inquest commences. This avoids
concerns.hazard: incomplete electronic records and delayed disclosure

concerns.quote: An initial full, updating letter was sent to Ellie's GP. However no further updating information was sent. A letter was written providing updating information, but this was not sent. No further updating information was sent to the GP by telephone, letter or email.
concerns.hazard: failure to maintain ongoing communication with GP

concerns.quote: The evidence heard is that efforts were made to contact the school by telephone. However, the school had no record of any such calls. There is no evidence of email or written correspondence or further telephone calls in an effort to communicate with the school.
It is accepted by the Trust that sharing of relevant information is necessary. NSFT has indicated it will
concerns.hazard: inadequate information sharing with external agencies

links.explanation: Both reports highlight failures in reliably communicating medication or updating information from the trust to a patient's GP. The earlier report points to missing automated notifications, while the later report describes missed manual updates.
